column1: # Where each gloss in lex-pt.tsv was read.
# lemma | pos | tgt | sources | quote | stands
# The gloss is the English word a Portuguese word is woven for, and the
# tooltip prints it back: it is the claim every reader meets first. Every
# other claim the pack makes about a word names its entry — genders in
# pt-genders.tsv, plurals in pt-plurals.tsv, verb forms in pt-verb-forms.tsv
# — and the gloss named none until 2026-10-08, the night fr-glosses.tsv and
# es-glosses.tsv were written the same way.
# Every row is read, all 356: the 178 nouns, 81 verbs, 57 adjectives, 22
# adverbs, 13 numerals and 5 interjections. Each was read in the rendered
# page of the word's English Wiktionary entry, in its Portuguese section: a
# script took the definition lines under each heading of the row's part of
# speech, examples, quotations and synonyms set aside, and drafted the first
# that holds the row's English word, and every quote was read against its
# page. Five drafts were another sense, and their lines quote the row's:
# dedo's first line holding "finger" is a unit of length, the width of one;
# ovo's is a cell, where the row is the egg with a shell; terra's is
# "ground", where "earth; soil" is the row's; trabalho's is "job; task",
# where "work; toil; labour" is; and pássaro's is "passerine", where its
# general sense, "(colloquial, somewhat proscribed) bird", is the row's.
# A page holds every word of one spelling, so a quote is from this word's
# own part of speech where the page has it. Three numerals are adjectives on
# theirs, and their lines quote those: cem, "hundred", mil, "thousand", and
# primeiro, "first". sozinho, woven for "alone" among the adverbs, has an
# adverb, and its line quotes it, though the page calls that use "(rare,
# nonstandard)": its adjective, "alone; by oneself", is the word's usual one.
# The title is the word as Wiktionary's address writes it, with an
# underscore for a space, so that each source stays one word of the field:
# wikt:pt:às_vezes. A noun cites the entry its gender was read in, which for
# every Portuguese noun is its own.
# Two pages name another form for the word the row weaves, so their lines
# quote the entry named and cite the word's own beside it, the quoted entry
# first. juntos is "masculine plural of junto", and its line quotes junto's
# adverb, "together (at the same time, in the same place)". And desculpa,
# woven for "sorry", is beside a noun — "excuse, pretext" and "apology" —
# the second-person imperative of desculpar, which is what a Portuguese
# speaker says it as; its line quotes desculpar's "(transitive) to forgive"
# and names "forgive" to stand for it, as la-glosses.tsv quotes Latin
# ignōsce. FORM_OF in tests/tools/glosses.test.ts lists both.
# Four phrases have no entry of their own, so each line cites the entries
# of its words and quotes a line of each, joined by " / ", naming no
# stand-in; COMPOSED in the test lists each with its words. estar de pé,
# "stand", is estar, "to be" of a passing state, and de pé, "up; standing",
# itself an entry of two words; estar em pé and ficar de pé have none.
# muitas vezes, "often", is muito, "much; many", and vez, "time; occasion" —
# its own words are inflected forms, muitas "feminine plural of muito" and
# vezes "plural of vez", so it cites the entries they are forms of; the one
# word frequentemente is "frequently, often". em todo lugar, "everywhere",
# and em nenhum lugar, "nowhere", are em, todo or nenhum, and lugar, and no
# variant tried has an entry: em toda parte, por toda parte, em todo lado,
# Blank where the quote holds the row's English word. Otherwise it names the
# word of the quote that stands for it, because the English word is not in
# the entry. Seven rows need one: vizinho for "neighbour" is "neighbor",
# pequeno for "little" "small", morno for "warm" "lukewarm, tepid", rápido
# for "quick" "fast", subir for "rise" "to ascend, to go up", dedo for
# "finger" "digit, a part of the body inclusive of fingers or toes", and
# desculpa for "sorry" "forgive", above. morno says less than "warm": the
# entry that gives "warm" is quente's, "hot, warm", which the pack weaves
# One row no definition gives. tarde, woven for "evening", is in its entry
# "afternoon" and nothing more; the adverb tarde is "late". Wiktionary's
# "evening" is serão, beside "overtime", and after dark it is noite, "night
# (period between sunset and sunrise)". QUEUED in tests/tools/glosses.test.ts
# names the row until it is taught differently; see TODO.md.
# tests/tools/glosses.test.ts requires every row of lex-pt.tsv to have a line
# here citing its own word's entry, whose quote holds its English word or the
# stand-in it names, and fails on a line outliving its row.

column5: person (an individual being, especially a human)
family; nuclear family (a father, mother and their sons and daughters)
mother (female who gives birth to or parents a child)
husband (male partner in a married couple)
queen (a monarch or the wife of a king)
neighbor (person who lives next to another)
(anatomy) mouth (the opening of a creature through which food is ingested)
nose (a protuberance on the face housing the nostrils, which are used to breathe or smell)
tooth (hard structure found in the jaws of most vertebrates)
blood (vital liquid flowing in human and animal bodies)
(anatomy) foot, part of the human body
digit, a part of the body inclusive of fingers or toes
skin (outer protective layer of the body of a person or animal)
(colloquial, somewhat proscribed) bird (any member of the class Aves, especially a small one)
fish (cold-blooded vertebrate animal that lives in water, moving with the help of fins and breathing with gills)
pig (the domesticated farm animal Sus scrofa)
bear (a member of the family Ursidae)
mouse (any rodent of the genus Mus)
snake; serpent (any reptile of the suborder Serpentes)
crow, raven (bird of the genus Corvus)
hound (dog breed with a good sense of smell developed for hunting)
milk (white liquid produced by the mammary glands)
salt (sodium chloride, a substance used as a condiment and preservative)
(biology) egg (rounded body produced by oviparous females consisting of a membrane and outer shell that contains the embryo)
(endearing) home (place or building where one dwells)
name (word or phrase which identifies an individual person, place, class, or thing)
key (object that opens and closes a lock)
bridge (construction or natural feature that spans a divide)
(countable) sword (a long bladed weapon with a grip and typically a pommel and crossguard (together forming a hilt), which is designed to cut, stab, slash and/or hack)
ring (round piece of metal worn around the finger)
sun; sunlight, sunshine (the light and heat which are received from the sun)
(astronomy) moon (any substantially sized natural satellite of a planet)
(astronomy) star (apparently fixed star that has its own light and heat)
earth; soil (mixture of sand and organic material found on the ground)
land; region; territory (area associated with something)

river (a large and often winding stream which drains a land mass, carrying water down from higher areas to a lower point, oftentimes ending in another body of water, such as an ocean or in an inland sea)
field (large open area, especially one where crops are grown or sports are played)
cloud (mass of dust, steam or smoke)
light (medium within which vision is possible)
(uncountable) time (the progression from the present into the future)
month (each of the twelve periods into which the year is divided)
winter (the coldest of the four seasons)
(uncountable) money (means of exchange and measure of value)
price (cost required to gain possession of something)
(uncountable) music (melodic and rhythmic sounds made as art)
fear (emotion caused by actual or perceived danger or threat)
anger (a strong feeling of displeasure, hostility or antagonism towards someone or something)
large; great; big (of great size or extent)
large; great; big (of great size or extent)
short (having a small distance between ends or edges)
old; ancient (having existed for a long period of time)
capable of producing great force; strong; forceful
fast (occurring or happening within a short time)
containing unpleasant substances such as dirt or grime; dirty; unclean
whole; entire; in full (with nothing missing)
to go (to move to a destination) [with para or a or em ‘to somewhere’; or with até ‘as far as somewhere’]
(intransitive) to come (to move towards the speaker or the agent)
(transitive) to see; to observe (to perceive with one’s eyes)
to think (communicate to oneself in one’s mind)
(transitive) to take (to get something into one’s possession or control)
(transitive, intransitive) to want; to wish; to desire
(transitive) to tell (to convey given information) [with que ‘that’]
to work (to do a specific task)
(transitive or intransitive) to play (to participate in a sport or game)
(intransitive) to run (to move quickly on one’s feet)
(intransitive) to walk (to move on one’s feet)
(intransitive) to speak; to talk (to say words out loud)
to read (to look at and interpret written information)
(intransitive) to sleep; to be asleep (to rest in a state of reduced consciousness)
(copulative) to be (denotes a transient quality; a quality expected to change) [with adjective] / up; standing (in an erect position)
(transitive) to love, to have great affection for
(intransitive, transitive) to fear (to feel fear about something)
(transitive) to hear (to perceive with the ear, without necessarily paying attention to it)
(transitive) to sense; to feel (to perceive by means of biological senses)
(transitive) to carry (to have in one’s immediate possession)
(ambitransitive) to break (end up or cause to end up in two or more pieces that cannot easily be reassembled)
(intransitive) to start; to begin; to commence
(transitive) to teach (to pass on knowledge to)
(intransitive or pronominal) to remember [with de ‘someone/something’ or de (+ personal infinitive) ‘to do something’]
to win (to achieve victory in a game, a war, etc)
to lose (an object, a job, interest etc.)
(intransitive or transitive) to fight (participate in a conflict) [with em or (less common) transitive ‘in a battle/conflict/etc.’]
(intransitive) to swim (support oneself and move on the surface or within a liquid, through coordinated movements of arms and legs)
(intransitive) to sing (express sounds musically through the voice)
(pronominal) to laugh (to express mirth or derision by emitting chuckling sounds) [with de ‘at someone/something’]
(intransitive) to cry; to weep (to shed tears from the eyes)
(transitive) to call; to summon (to ask someone to come)
(formal, intransitive) to depart; to leave; to go away
to follow (to go or come after in physical space)
(transitive) to search; to seek; to look for [with direct object or por ‘for something’]
to change (to become or cause to become something different)
to fall; to fall down; to drop
(transitive) to cut (to split using a sharp instrument)

sometimes (on certain occasions, but not always)
now; right now (at the present time)

together (at the same time, in the same place)
(rare, nonstandard) alone; by oneself; on one's own
in; at (located in a location) / every; all (all of a group) / place (a location or position)
in; at (located in a location) / no, none / place (a location or position)
very; a lot; very much (to a great extent or degree)
please (interjection to make commands more polite)
